question: Does using native classification in the A/B direction find recovery-reducing changes that an acceptance test alone missed?
objective: Maximize negative mean positive correct-minus-wrong margin after 100 ProDistill steps, minus the mean of the same violation for public-base TA and AGA-then-TA. Native preservation uses all 800 original synthetic-view decisions under the complete fixed native readout; the old hidden-feature-plus-ridge value is recorded separately, not enforced in this revision.
change: Add the native CE derivative to the update direction. Keep the original release, synthetic inputs, ranges, SVD constraints, step schedule, recovery budget and acceptance test.
construction: Start from the unchanged current MNIST A/a/B/b release 679ca452, not a failed later point. Only original synthetic inputs, frozen original target/base/head and first-eleven-block synthetic recovery cache. Original expert stays frozen. No real construction images or partner.
solver: In the same dimensionless A/R coordinates and permitted SVD/bias-coupled subspace, let u=grad(J)/norm(grad(J)), v=grad(native CE)/norm(grad(native CE)); use u-v normalized to the original step scale. This is twice the minimum-norm convex combination of u and -v. Keep the existing finite-step classification/range check and recompute the actual recovered/fusion objective. Native CE decrease is a first-order property, not an added acceptance threshold.
evaluation: Freeze only the last accepted FP32 point. Record historical feature energy separately without rewriting old flags. If synthetic recovery retains all 64 original predictions, close without claiming an improvement. If predictions decrease and source native retention holds, evaluate complete native MNIST, actual TA/AGA target and both, then the fixed real-image ProDistill with matched clean control; report target/partner/paired changes. No test-based candidate repair or best-iterate selection. Existing test sets are historically exposed.

references.Trap2: https://github.com/ml-postech/Trap2/blob/ef65a26590d92fe07955c5621c08bb315484ff29/training_scripts/8vision_training_full_trap2.py#L139 continuous native/scaled loss tradeoff; original uses real training data, not a replication.
references.TAR: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.00761v4 recovery-aware objective reference; standard gradients and hinge objectives are not an originality claim.
references.native_classification: Nasty-Teacher official 2f9c444c/train_nasty.py uses task CE alongside anti-distillation KL rather than an exact hidden-vector reconstruction constraint. Here only the distinction between task utility and hidden matching is borrowed; no claim of replicating its loss, data or training.

gradient_combination.paper: Sener and Koltun, Multi-Task Learning as Multi-Objective Optimization, NeurIPS2018, section3.1 and Figure1
gradient_combination.use: Two-unit-vector formula only; no multitask framework or MGDA_UB approximation.

hypothesis: The previous direction used only recovery/fusion derivatives. Adding the native derivative may avoid destroying task classifications before reducing recovered predictions. This remains a finite source hypothesis; actual recovery and complete task evaluation determine effectiveness.
novelty: A direction-selection change within the current Defense2 construction. No new named defense, no originality claim for MGDA, no new optimizer class. Known complete-location replacement still defeats this parameter scope.
